tables.caption: Maturity assessment vs market ranking
rows: Prototype maturity against a capability rubric — yes. Market rank among commercial products — no: NyaySutra has no users, pricing or deployment, and most competitors' AI could not be tested.
4.95 / 10 on the weighted rubric (100% of criteria evidenced, confidence Medium). Strongest: guardrails, routing, workflow breadth. Weakest: corpus, case law, maturity.

Tier 3 of 4 — 'Advanced prototype / pre-commercial'. Tier 1 = national incumbents (SCC Online, Manupatra, Indian Kanoon, LexisNexis); Tier 2 = funded AI-native products with users (CaseMine, Bharat.Law, NyayAssist, Lexlegis); Tier 3 = working prototypes with real architecture; Tier 4 = demos.
Why no India-wide or global rank
Competitor AI accuracy is unmeasured in public (except a 2024 US study of Lexis/Westlaw, S20); we could not sign in to any competitor; vendor claims dominate. A rank would be invented.
Bharat.Law (price, languages), Indian Kanoon PRISM (free tier), NyayAssist (research + workflow for small chambers).

sections.title: 14. Unique selling proposition and target market

tables.caption: Positioning
rows: A bilingual, free-to-start legal assistant for Indian advocates whose every citation is machine-checked against the source text, combined with matter, calendar and drafting workflow.
Solo advocates and small chambers in district and High Courts (Maharashtra first), who cannot afford ₹50k+/yr subscriptions
Law students and legal-aid clinics (free tier); NGOs and legal-aid authorities
Large firms needing full case-law databases and enterprise contracts (Harvey, Lexis, SCC)
'Research you can verify, and your practice in one place — in English and Hindi.'
